lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Comet Marimba! One oh two point two! Hold on to your hat!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: You're catching rays on Comet Marimba. Tropical grooves at seventy kilometres a second!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Good morning from the beach on the tail of a comet! This is Comet Marimba!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Comet Marimba, under a sky full of stars all going the other way.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Comet Marimba. Out of office. Permanently.

lines.speaker: DJ Sunglass Crab
lines.text: Comet Marimba.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Thank you, Crab! He's so cool.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Sun, sand, and a very fast tail. You're on Comet Marimba.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Surf report! Waves of pure time rolling in at three to four minutes, nice and glassy, with the occasional Tuesday breaking on the left.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: If you get caught in one, just relax. You'll come out last week. Totally fine.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Hat update! We have lost eleven hats since breakfast. They're somewhere behind us now, in orbit.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: If you're further back on the comet and a sun hat hits you, that's ours. Keep it. Wear it with love.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Big shout-out to the crab on the decks, who has refused every single request today.

lines.speaker: DJ Sunglass Crab
lines.text: Click.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: That's a no. He's an artist. Here's what he wants to play.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: This beach is sponsored by Grumbel's Ladders! Want to see over the tail? Grumbel's! Want to touch a passing star? Grumbel's!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Want to get back down safely? Grumbel's, probably! Up is a choice, everyone! Down is a vacation!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Good morning, beach people! The sun's a friendly distance away, the hammock is stable, and someone has left a coconut in the ice tail to chill. It's going to be a great day! It's always a great day!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: The sun is setting! Well. We're leaving it behind. Same effect! Everybody turn around and wave goodbye to the sun! Bye, sun! See you in seventy-six years!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Night on the comet. The stars are streaking past so fast they look like rain. Warm rain. Lie back in the hammock and let it fall on you. Here's a slow one.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Someone asked me how long I've been on vacation. You know when you go away, and you forget what day it is? I forgot what year it is. I forgot when I forgot.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Best decision I ever made. I think. Here's a song!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Sunscreen reminder! Factor four thousand on the face, factor nine thousand on the tail side. Reapply every time we go round the sun. That's about every seventy-six years, so set a reminder!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Lovely surprise on the beach today: a shadow, all on his own, lying on a towel. Name's Greg! He's working on his tan, which for a shadow means getting lighter.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Go on, Greg! Hollis says send a postcard!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Midday on the comet! Everybody grab a drink with a tiny umbrella in it. If you don't have a drink, just hold the tiny umbrella. It's the umbrella that matters.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Fun fact! The beach is moving at seventy kilometres a second, but the sand doesn't care, and neither should you. That's the whole secret to vacation. Here's another one!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: That last track had a marimba carved from driftwood that drifted four billion miles to get here. Talk about commitment! Talk about a commute! Here's another.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Okay! For the first time ever, the crab has a request.

lines.speaker: DJ Sunglass Crab
lines.text: Play the marimba one.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: They're all marimba ones, Crab.

lines.speaker: DJ Sunglass Crab
lines.text: Play it anyway.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: You heard him!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: If you're stuck in an office listening to this, hello! This one's for you. Close your eyes. Feel the sand. Feel the speed.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Ignore the email. The email can wait. The email is in another galaxy.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Late night beach check. Hammock: swaying. Crab: asleep in his sunglasses. Me: thinking about how lucky we are to be going this fast, together, somewhere nobody's ever been. Night, everyone.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: We've got a call from, it says here, a lift? Hello!

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Hello, love. It's Bev. I'm in a lift. Is this the request line?

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: It sure is! Why are you in a lift?

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: It's where I heard my song. It goes, da da dum, da da. I thought, if I get back in a lift, it might come on again.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Has it?

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: No. But this marimba's very nice.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Stay in the lift, Bev! We'll keep it nice for you!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: It's Hammock Hours on Comet Marimba! Lie back. The stars are going past like warm rain.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: The crab's asleep in his sunglasses. The hammock's swaying. Somebody left a coconut in the ice tail to chill, and it's perfect now.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: I'm going to drink it. Here's a slow one.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Late night thought. We're going seventy kilometres a second, but if you lie very still in the hammock, it feels like we're not moving at all.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: I think that's the secret. Of comets. And of everything.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: It's Sunset on the Tail! Everybody turn round and wave! Bye, sun!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Sunset report! The sun's a lovely orange tonight, and getting smaller, because we're leaving it. Honestly the most relaxing way to watch a sunset.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: You don't have to do anything. It just goes.

lines.speaker: DJ Sunglass Crab
lines.text: Play the sunset one.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: They're all sunset ones at sunset, Crab!

lines.speaker: DJ Sunglass Crab
lines.text: Play it anyway.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: You heard him! The crab has spoken! Twice in one week!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Comet Marimba! Still on vacation! Still going very fast!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Ooh, that one had sand in it! Lovely!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Hi, beach people! Coco here, horizontal, as usual!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Morning on the comet! The sun's a friendly distance away!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Hat update! Fourteen hats lost since lunch. One of them came all the way back round, on a different person. They looked great. We let them keep it.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Los Perihelios are playing a set at the far end of the beach tonight! They only play when we're near the sun, so this is it, folks! Next gig in seventy six years! Get there early!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: The crab has refused another request.

lines.speaker: DJ Sunglass Crab
lines.text: Click.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: That's a no. Somebody asked for something with a saxophone. The crab doesn't believe in saxophones.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Surf report! Waves of pure time, four minutes high, glassy, with the occasional Thursday. If you wipe out, you'll come out on Monday. Totally fine! Mondays are lovely here!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: The Hammock Syndicate have a new album, and they recorded the whole thing lying down. You can hear it. Some of it is snoring. It's the best bit.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Reminder! The tide on this beach goes out every seventy six years. So if you left a towel by the water, it's fine. It'll be fine for ages!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Here's another one! Bare feet only, please! Sandals by the door!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Here's a breezy one! Hold on to your hat! Too late!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Crab! Drop the next one!

lines.speaker: DJ Sunglass Crab
lines.text: Click.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: He dropped it!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Here comes the marimba! It's always the marimba!

clips.title: Greg Comes Home, Part Two: Hitching a Comet

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Okay, beach people! We picked up a passenger in lane twelve! He hopped across from a whale ship at four this morning! Say hi, Greg!

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Hello. Sorry. I'm very sandy.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Everybody's sandy! That's the beach! Crab, get the man some sunglasses!

lines.speaker: DJ Sunglass Crab
lines.text: Click.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: The crab has given Greg sunglasses! The crab has never given anyone anything! Greg, that's huge!

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: They're very small. They fit, though. When you're a shadow, everything fits.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: So where are you headed?

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Home. The eastern Overlap. Is the comet going that way?

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Sort of! But we only come round every seventy six years, so you'll have to jump off at exactly the right moment. Too early, you're in space. Too late, you're in seventy six years.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: When's the right moment?

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: When the moon goes past on the left! Big grey one, sleepy face, speakers on it. Jump for the moon. The moon's always got room.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Hey, Greg. Why did you leave, in the first place?

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: He never went anywhere. I wanted to see things.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: I've seen things now. I want to tell him about them.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: That's the best reason to go home I've ever heard! And I've never gone home!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: There it is! The moon! Go, Greg! Jump!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: He's off! He's flying! He's waving! He's still wearing the crab's sunglasses!

lines.speaker: DJ Sunglass Crab
lines.text: Keep them.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: It's Halloween on the beach, and the crab has dressed up! He's taken his sunglasses off!

lines.speaker: DJ Sunglass Crab
lines.text: Click.

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: He's come as a crab without sunglasses! Nobody recognises him! It's genuinely unsettling!

lines.speaker: Coco Halley
lines.text: Comet Marimba! Halloween on the tail! Spooky, sandy, and very, very fast!
